title: Oklahoma State University men's basketball team plane crash
summary: A King Air carrying an Oklahoma State basketball team and broadcasters crashed near Denver during descent in snow and darkness. The pilot lost electrical power and most cockpit instruments in instrument meteorological conditions. The investigation found the pilot became spatially disoriented and lost control of the aircraft, entering a steep graveyard spiral that was unrecoverable. The co-pilot, though present, lacked King Air type training.
probable_cause: The pilot's spatial disorientation resulting from failure to maintain positive manual control of the airplane with available flight instrumentation. A contributing factor was loss of AC electrical power during instrument meteorological conditions, which disabled most pilot-side instruments including the altimeter, attitude indicator, and horizontal situation indicator.

crash occurred at 19:37 EST (evening)

title: Thai Airways International 114
summary: An explosion originated in the center fuel tank while cabin crew prepared a Boeing 737-400 for boarding at Don Mueang International Airport in Bangkok. Investigators determined that flammable fuel-air mixture inside the center tank ignited from sparks generated by an activated fuel pump with metal shavings present. The center tank contained approximately 80 kg of residual fuel and could reach temperatures as high as 48 degrees Celsius with air conditioning packs on, creating flammable conditions.
probable_cause: Flammable fuel-air mixture in the center wing fuel tank ignited from sparks generated from an activated fuel pump in the presence of metal shavings in the tank.

aircraft.type: de Havilland Canada DHC-6-300 Twin Otter

summary: De Havilland DHC-6 Twin Otter Flight 1501 took off from Princess Juliana International Airport at 4:00 pm on 24 March 2001 in good weather. During approach to Gustaf III Airport at Saint Barthélemy, while flying above the western slope of La Tourmente Pass, the aircraft banked steeply to the left. It rapidly lost altitude and crashed into a house, killing all 19 people aboard and one elderly man on the ground. Investigation revealed the captain accidentally moved one engine's thrust lever into the beta range, creating severe thrust asymmetry.
probable_cause: Crew error in managing the plane's thrust lever, causing one engine to enter reverse beta range and creating thrust asymmetry that induced steep left bank. This was the first fatal Twin Otter accident where accidental thrust selection caused propeller to enter the beta range.

events.text: Flight 1501 took off from Princess Juliana International Airport at 4:00 pm local time using visual flight rules in good weather.

The aircraft crashed onto a house with a massive explosion, killing all 19 aboard and one man on the ground.

title: 2001 Avjet Gulfstream III crash
summary: A chartered Gulfstream III operated by Avjet crashed into terrain near Aspen on March 29, 2001. The captain conducted a premature descent below the minimum descent altitude without runway in sight. Pressure from the charter customer and tight curfew constraints contributed. The NTSB found the crew's operation of the airplane below minimum descent altitude without required visual references was the probable cause.
probable_cause: The flight crew's operation of the airplane below the minimum descent altitude without the required visual references.

title: Vladivostok Air 352
summary: Vladivostok Air Flight 352, a Tupolev Tu-154M, crashed near Irkutsk on 4 July 2001 while approaching Irkutsk Airport. During approach, the first officer made erroneous control inputs including a nose-down input that disconnected the autopilot. The aircraft entered an excessive left bank of up to 48 degrees. Both pilots made alternating control inputs attempting recovery, and excessive nose-up input by both pilots induced an aerodynamic stall at insufficient altitude. The aircraft entered a corkscrew and crashed into farmland, killing all 145 aboard.
probable_cause: Russian investigation committee MAK attributed the causes to pilot error. During the approach, the crew made erroneous input on the aircraft's yoke, causing the airspeed to deplete. A series of errors caused the yoke to be excessively pulled, causing the aircraft to enter a corkscrew. The crew tried to recover but failed due to the aircraft's insufficient altitude.

events.text: The flight took off from Yekaterinburg Koltsovo Airport at 19:47 local time and climbed to its cruising altitude of 10,000 m.
While the turn was being carried out by the crew, the bank angle suddenly increased and the first officer made a nose down input of -4 degree and a left bank input into the steering column.
A warning sounded as the first officer's input caused the autopilot to disconnect and the bank angle to increase from 20 degree to 30 degree.
Captain Goncharuk noticed the increasing bank angle and took over the control to correct the situation but the bank angle continued to increase up to 48 degrees.
The crew sensed an increase of the aircraft's vertical rate of descent and put an excessive nose up input into the yoke causing the aircraft to enter an aerodynamic stall at a severe left bank angle.
The aircraft crashed with its belly first near the settlement of Burdakovka, approximately 22 km from Irkutsk, and immediately exploded upon impact, instantly killing all 145 passengers and crew.

title: Rus 9633
summary: An Ilyushin Il-76TD cargo flight crashed on 14 July 2001 a few seconds after takeoff from Chkalovsky Airport near Moscow. The aircraft was loaded 14 tons above its maximum takeoff weight of 191.9 tons due to a weighing error, with the actual weight approximately 204 tons. The pilots did not perform center-of-gravity calculations. During takeoff rotation, the aircraft immediately listed to the left, and at 23 meters altitude the pilots shifted the horizontal stabilizer nose-down at 5.4 degrees to -3.9 degrees, which is forbidden during takeoff. This caused the aircraft to descend, and when the commander pulled back on the elevator, the aircraft could not recover and struck terrain 530 meters past the runway.
probable_cause: Improper weight and balance causing unstable takeoff, compounded by prohibited modulation of horizontal stabilizer during takeoff which dropped the nose and made recovery impossible at low altitude.

title: 2001 Marsh Harbour Cessna 402 crash
summary: The Cessna 402B crashed shortly after takeoff from Marsh Harbour Airport, killing all nine on board. The aircraft was overloaded by more than 900 lb and carried eight passengers exceeding the certified maximum of seven. The pilot, Luis Morales III, had falsified his FAA license and flight experience records, and toxicology revealed cocaine and alcohol in his system. The overloaded aircraft with excessive aft center of gravity lost control during takeoff.

title: Binter Mediterráneo 8261
summary: Binter Mediterráneo Flight 8261 received a false fire warning for the port engine on approach to Málaga. The first officer, lacking simulator training, erroneously shut down both engines while attempting to follow emergency procedures. The aircraft descended without power and crashed 200 meters short of the runway threshold, killing the captain and three passengers.
probable_cause: The accident resulted from the first officer's incorrect execution of the engine fire emergency procedure, shutting down both engines instead of only the indicated engine. The co-pilot had not received simulator training in emergency procedures from the airline, and incomplete maintenance procedures led to the false fire alarm.

Lead hijacker Hani Hanjour, who had undergone extensive flight training, took control, disengaged the autopilot at 9:29 a.m. and flew a 330-degree spiral turn before crashing the Boeing 757 into the west side of the Pentagon at 09:37, killing all 64 aboard and 125 in the building and igniting a large fire.

title: Siberia Airlines 1812
summary: Siberia Airlines Flight 1812 was shot down over the Black Sea by an S-200 air defense missile fired by Ukrainian forces during joint Ukrainian-Russian military air-defense exercises at Cape Opuk in Crimea. The aircraft was cruising at 36,000 feet when Russian ground control lost contact. Ukrainian officials initially denied responsibility but later acknowledged that a Ukrainian S-200 missile had been launched seaward and locked onto the passenger aircraft instead of its intended target drone, with the missile detonating 15 meters above the aircraft, destroying it completely.
probable_cause: The aircraft was struck by an S-200 surface-to-air missile fired by Ukrainian armed forces during military training exercises. The missile, which had overshot its intended target drone and should have self-destructed, instead locked onto the passenger aircraft and detonated, destroying the aircraft and killing all 78 people on board.

title: 2001 Linate Airport runway collision
summary: During heavy fog with visibility less than 200 meters, a Cessna Citation business jet taxied along the wrong route and crossed an active runway where an MD-87 had just been cleared for takeoff. The aircraft collided at 150 knots, and the MD-87 departed the runway to strike a luggage hangar at 136 knots. All occupants of both aircraft and four ground personnel were killed. The investigation found the immediate cause was the Cessna's incursion but revealed systemic failures: no functional ground radar, obscured taxiway signs, deactivated motion-sensing alarms, and poor phraseology matching between ATC and airport signage.
probable_cause: The immediate cause was the incursion of the Cessna aircraft onto the active runway. However, the accident resulted from multiple systemic failures including the absence of a functioning ground radar system, obscured or worn taxiway signs, deactivated runway incursion alarms, and incompatible ATC terminology.

The aircraft deviated from its planned route to avoid weather around 10:38 before losing radio and radar contact. Total electrical failure caused by lightning strike rendered elevators, lighting, instruments, anti-ice and navigation systems inoperable, resulting in spatial disorientation and impact with the Mediterranean Sea at steep pitch angle.

title: American Airlines 587
summary: American Airlines Flight 587, an Airbus A300 bound for Santo Domingo, crashed into Belle Harbor, Queens shortly after taking off from JFK on November 12, 2001, killing 265. The NTSB found First Officer Molin's aggressive alternating rudder inputs during wake turbulence from a preceding Japan Airlines 747 overstressed the vertical stabilizer until it separated, causing a flat spin and loss of control; both engines then sheared off.

title: Crossair 3597
summary: A Crossair Avro RJ100 crashed into a wooded hilltop near Bassersdorf, 4 kilometers short of Zurich runway 28, killing 24 of the 33 aboard. The aircraft was switched from an ILS approach to runway 14 to a less accurate VOR/DME approach to runway 28 due to a Swiss noise abatement regulation. Captain Lutz, despite a history of navigation errors not addressed by the operator, failed to properly plan and execute the VOR/DME approach, descending the aircraft below minimum descent altitude and off the assigned track.
